artifact_review:
The Router reported no artifacts, which aligns with my visual inspection. The topology_boundary_auditor provided a high confidence score (0.955) for the water-duck interface, confirming clean boundaries without melting or haloing. The perceptual_quality_auditor found no noise or blur. 

However, the animal_pose_auditor reported a 'HIGH' artifact risk due to an 82% low-confidence keypoint ratio. Per the system instructions, I must treat this as a WEAK signal caused by domain shift (ViTPose trained on real photos vs. AI generation) unless visually confirmed. Upon close inspection of the regions with low-confidence keypoints (faces, limbs), I see NO structural anomalies, fusion, or extra limbs. The anatomy is biologically plausible. Therefore, I disregard the pose auditor's warning as a false positive driven by texture/style differences rather than structural failure.
